privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This app is a small family project. Here is exactly what it keeps, and why.
privacy.who: A parent built it for their own children and shares it for free. There are no ads, and nothing is sold. To look after the app, the person who runs it can see how many families and children use it, and each child’s practice; this is never shared.
privacy.stored: For parents: your email, a scrambled (hashed) password, and the public half of any passkey you add. For each child: the avatar, colour and settings, and their practice: each answer, how long it took, hints, lessons and the optional “how did that feel?” taps. A child who starts on their own gives no name, email or age: the age they tap only picks the starting settings and isn’t kept. A parent may add a first name or nickname, and a birth year. For each phone: a random code that keeps the child signed in (also kept in a cookie, so the child isn’t lost if the browser clears its storage), the browser’s short device description, and when it was last used.
privacy.notStored: Children have no emails or passwords, and no sign-in. There are no analytics, no trackers and no advertising. There are two cookies: the parent sign-in, and the child’s phone code. Nothing is used to contact a child or to build a profile of them beyond their maths practice. The only outside script is Cloudflare Turnstile, a check against automated sign-ups, loaded only on the screens where a child starts, a parent signs up or a password is reset; it sees the browser’s network address and type, as Cloudflare’s Turnstile privacy addendum describes. English read-aloud uses the phone’s own built-in voice; the Arabic voice is recorded and comes with the app. Nothing your child says is recorded.
privacy.phone: Practice is saved on the phone first, so it works offline, then copied to our server. Unlinking a phone clears its copy the next time it connects.
privacy.keep: A child nobody has connected to a parent account is deleted automatically: after 7 days if they never practised, otherwise after a year without practice. Everything else stays until you delete it.
privacy.where: On Cloudflare (Workers and a D1 database in Western Europe), which hosts the app. If password-reset email is turned on, your email address is passed to the email service only to send that message.
privacy.delete: Remove one child under that child’s Settings, or everything with “Delete my account” at the bottom of the parent area. Deletion is immediate and permanent. A child with no parent account is removed automatically, as above.
privacy.contact: Open an issue at github.com/xenastro/ashra, where the app’s code is public.

help.title: How Ashra works
help.intro: Ashra’s goal is instant recall: seeing 7 × 8 and simply knowing 56, without counting. It gets there with a few minutes a day, mostly questions your child can already answer, and by bringing each fact back just before it would be forgotten.
help.facts:
3 × 7 and 7 × 3 are the same fact, so the 10 × 10 table is only 55 facts. Practice asks both ways round, but they share one record and one cell on the map. That is why the map is a mirror image.
×1 and ×10 are taught as rules, and ×2, ×5 and ×9 as patterns. That leaves about 15 truly hard facts, and each comes with a way to work it out (×4 is double, then double again).
help.checkup:
Before daily practice starts, a check-up finds out what your child already knows. It is framed as “let’s see what you know”, not as a test.
• It starts with 5 easy questions, like 1 × 4 and 10 × 3. They measure how fast your child types on this phone, which sets their own line for “fast” (see Speed, quietly). If all of them are quick, the rest of ×1 and ×10 is counted as known.
• Then it asks each fact once, from easy to hard.
• Right and fast: the fact starts at Know it. Right but slow: Learning, because your child knows it but works it out. Wrong: it stays at Not yet, to be taught later with a guide.
• Two misses in a row within one table skip the rest of that table, so your child isn’t worn down. Those facts stay at Not yet too.
• A break is offered every 25 questions, and the check-up can be finished another day.
For a younger learner, the check-up covers only ×1, ×10, ×2 and ×5.
help.session:
After the check-up, “Start today’s practice” builds a session of about 30 answers (20 for a younger learner; see Session length in Settings). Questions are picked in this order:
• Reviews: facts your child knows whose waiting time is up, the longest-waiting first.
• Learning facts: ones your child is still working out.
• New facts: up to 3 a session (2 for a younger learner). Each starts with a step-by-step guide your child types through, then comes back about 3, 6 and 10 questions later.
• Known facts in between, as easy wins.
Harder questions (new, learning, or just missed) take turns with easier ones, so most answers are successes. Each fact is shown either way round at random, 7 × 3 or 3 × 7.
• No more new facts are added once accuracy falls below 85% (after the first 6 answers), while more than 2 hard facts are still waiting, or in the last 6 questions.
• After a mistake, the right answer is shown and the fact comes back 2 and then 5 questions later.
• A fact answered right but slowly comes back once, a few questions later.
• No fact is asked more than 6 times in one session.
• From the 5th question, a known fact is sometimes asked as ? × 7 = 56, at most 4 times a session (3 for a younger learner).
• The session always ends on a right answer, going a few questions over if a retry is still waiting.
help.order:
New facts follow the usual school order, in groups:
• First: ×1, ×10 and ×2
• Then: ×5
• Then: ×4, ×3 and ×8
• Then: ×9, ×6 and ×7
• Bonus: ×11 and ×12
Each fact belongs to the easier of its two tables and is taught with that table’s method: 7 × 5 is a ×5 fact (half of 7 × 10), and 4 × 9 is a ×9 fact. Within a group, smaller facts come first, and facts left at Not yet in an earlier group always come before later ones.
The next group opens once 70% of the current group is at Getting there or above.
With Table size set to “10×10, then unlock ×11 & ×12”, the bonus rows open once every 10 × 10 fact has been started and 80% of them are at Know it or above.
help.levels: Every fact has a level from 0 to 5. The level sets its colour on the map and when it is asked again:
help.levelsMore:
• Right and fast, when the fact is due: up one level. A new fact moves to Learning on its first right answer.
• Right but slow: it stays where it is and is asked again soon.
• Wrong: back to Learning. A slip on a fact known well (level 4 or 5) only goes back to Getting there, since it is often a typo.
• Answers given with a hint or a guide never count as fast.
• Seeing a fact before it is due, as an easy filler, doesn’t move it up. A mistake there still counts.
So the quickest way from new to Mastered takes about 11 days: right and fast in the session it is taught, then again 1, 3 and 7 days later. After that, a Mastered fact is checked every 3 weeks.
help.speed:
Your child never sees a timer or a countdown. Time is recorded only to tell instant recall from counting.
“Fast” means within your child’s own line: how long they take to type an answer they know cold (measured in the check-up), plus 2.5 seconds, kept between 2.5 and 12 seconds. “What counts as fast” in Settings makes it a bit stricter or gives more time. Bilingual mode adds another 2.5 seconds for reading the Arabic words.
While a question is read aloud, the clock waits.
help.dashboard:
• Fact map: grey is Not yet, which means not started. It may never have been asked, or it was missed or skipped in the check-up. Amber is Learning or Getting there. The greens go from Know it (light) to Mastered (deep). Tap a fact to see its last answers and the guide that teaches it.
• Fluent facts: how many facts are at Know it or above.
• Facts that need help: facts with at least 2 recent answers where one of the last 10 was wrong, or the typical time is slower than your child’s “fast” line. Up to 6, the hardest first.
• Accuracy and typical answer time: check-up and practice answers from the last 7 days. The time is the middle value of right answers; the arrow compares it with the 7 days before.
• Missing-number puzzles are counted on their own and never change the map.
• How sessions felt: the optional check-in at the end of each session.
help.games: After the check-up, your child can also play Find the pairs and Fill a row. There are no timers and no losing. Games are for fun and extra practice: they don’t change any fact’s level.
help.mapNew: Not started. It may never have been asked, or it was missed or skipped in the check-up. It is taught with a guide when its turn comes.
help.mapLearning: Being worked on: answered right but slowly, or missed recently. Asked again in the same session or the next day.
help.mapFluent: Answered right and fast, within your child’s own time, not just correct. Reviewed after 3, then 7 days, and the green gets deeper each time.
help.mapMastered: Stayed fast across reviews spread over more than a week. Checked every 3 weeks.
help.mapNote: One wrong answer moves a fact back to amber. Here you see the answers from amber up; your child sees them only once a fact is green.

install.title: Put Ashra on the home screen
install.intro: Then Ashra opens like an app: full screen, from its own icon. It also keeps the practice saved on the phone safer, since browsers can clear websites’ data but not an app’s.
install.already: ✓ Ashra is already on this phone’s home screen.
install.onComputer: These steps are for a phone. Open this page on the phone itself: copy the link below and send it there.
install.done: ✓ Done! Ashra is on the home screen. It may take a few seconds to appear.
install.installNote: Your phone will ask you to confirm.
install.useChrome: This is easiest in Chrome: open this page there, then:
install.chrome1: Tap ⋮ at the top right of Chrome.
install.chrome2: Tap “Add to Home screen”. On some phones it says “Install app”.
install.chrome3: Tap “Install”. Ashra’s icon appears on the home screen after a few seconds.
install.samsung3: Tap “Add”. Ashra’s icon appears on the home screen.
install.useSafari: This only works well in Safari: open this page there, then:
install.safari1: Tap ⋯ next to the address. If you see the Share button (a square with an arrow) instead, tap that and skip the next step.
install.safari3: Scroll down and tap “Add to Home Screen”. Not in the list? Tap “Edit Actions” at the very bottom and add it.
install.safari4: If you see “Open as Web App”, leave it on. Then tap “Add” at the top right.
install.safariTip: Opened the link from WhatsApp, Messages or Mail and can’t find these buttons? Tap the compass icon to open the page in Safari first.
install.iosChrome1: Tap the Share button (a square with an arrow) at the top right, next to the address.
install.iosChrome2: Scroll down and tap “Add to Home Screen”.
install.inAppTitle: Open it in the phone’s browser first
install.inAppIos: This page is open inside another app, which can’t add it to the home screen. Tap ⋯ or the compass icon and choose “Open in Safari” (or “Open in browser”). Or copy the link and paste it into Safari.
install.inAppAndroid: This page is open inside another app, which can’t add it to the home screen. Tap ⋮ and choose “Open in Chrome” (or “Open in browser”). Or copy the link and paste it into Chrome.
